body.purpose: Recipes, controls, lists, navigation, and instructions.

label.purpose: Meal labels, dates, quantities, and concise orientation.

shadows.name: temporary-overlay
shadows.purpose: Menus and temporary sheets that sit above the working document.

motion.name: media-wait
motion.purpose: Loading treatment for on-demand recipe media.

components.name: Primary Action
components.description: The one highest-value action in the active household task.
components.css: .ds-primary-action { min-height: 44px; padding: 10px 14px; border: 1px solid #476346; border-radius: 8px; background: #476346; color: #FCFBF7; font: 650 1rem ui-sans-serif, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", sans-serif; letter-spacing: -.01em; } .ds-primary-action:hover { background: color-mix(in srgb, #476346 88%, #272823); } .ds-primary-action:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid color-mix(in srgb, #2F58B8 55%, white); outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Ghost Action
components.description: A visible secondary action that stays quiet beside the primary decision.
components.css: .ds-ghost-action { min-height: 44px; padding: 10px 14px; border: 1px solid #D9D6CC; border-radius: 8px; background: transparent; color: #272823; font: 650 1rem ui-sans-serif, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", sans-serif; letter-spacing: -.01em; } .ds-ghost-action:hover { border-color: #272823; } .ds-ghost-action:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid color-mix(in srgb, #2F58B8 55%, white); outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Working Field
components.description: A practical, readable field for household food information.
components.css: .ds-working-field { width: 100%; min-height: 44px; padding: 10px 12px; border: 1px solid #D9D6CC; border-radius: 8px; background: #FCFBF7; color: #272823; font: 1rem ui-sans-serif, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", sans-serif; } .ds-working-field:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid color-mix(in srgb, #2F58B8 55%, white); outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Meal Period Chapter
components.description: A flat, tonal breakfast, lunch, or dinner section that makes Day → Meal → Recipe scannable.
components.css: .ds-meal-period { display: grid; gap: 8px; padding: 24px 16px; border-top: 1px solid #D9D6CC; background: #FCFBF7; color: #272823; } .ds-meal-period p { margin: 0; color: #666960; font: 600 .78rem ui-sans-serif, sans-serif; } .ds-meal-period strong { font: 500 1.55rem Iowan Old Style, "Palatino Linotype", Palatino, Georgia, serif; } .ds-meal-period button { width: fit-content; min-height: 44px; padding: 0; border: 0; background: transparent; color: #476346; font: 650 1rem ui-sans-serif, sans-serif; } .ds-meal-period button:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid color-mix(in srgb, #2F58B8 55%, white); outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Core Navigation
components.description: The stable four-destination navigation, fixed safely above the mobile device edge.
components.css: .ds-core-nav { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(4, 1fr); padding: 8px 12px; background: #282B25; } .ds-core-nav button { min-width: 0; min-height: 48px; padding: 6px 2px; border: 0; border-radius: 6px; background: transparent; color: #D5D7CE; font: 650 .82rem ui-sans-serif, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", sans-serif; } .ds-core-nav .ds-active { background: #FCFBF7; color: #272823; } .ds-core-nav button:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #FCFBF7; outline-offset: -1px; }

narrative.overview: Ryan Family Menu is a smart household food concierge, not meal-planning software. It makes a family's food situation recognizable in the few seconds available between school pickup, a grocery aisle, and starting dinner: what the family is eating, what is still undecided, and what needs attention next. The visual character is warm, editorial, calm, and exact: mineral canvas, ceramic-paper surfaces, herb action, clay attention, and quiet seams borrow the calm material clarity of a working kitchen without becoming literal kitchen décor.
keyCharacteristics: Recognition and scanning win over instruction, especially in the first 2–3 seconds.
The current household food state is more important than planning mechanics.
Editorial serif headings and quiet paper surfaces make ordinary family content feel considered.
Progressive emphasis makes the next decision clear without falsifying the complete state.
English and Spanish are one product experience, not separate workflows.

rules.name: The State-First Color Rule
rules.body: Color clarifies a real state or a broad reading chapter; it never substitutes for labels, hierarchy, or navigation.

rules.name: The Three-Level Rule
rules.body: In planning, Day → Meal → Recipe must never collapse into equal visual weight. Day boundaries orient; meal headings group; recipe names read as the content belonging to that meal.

rules.name: The Busy-Moment Rule
rules.body: Every major screen must have a dominant answer to the question that caused the user to open it. Prefer recognition and direct state over explanatory copy or disconnected widgets.

rules.name: The Safe-Edge Rule
rules.body: Fixed navigation, status areas, and sticky actions reserve space using system safe-area insets. Scrollable content and focused controls must clear the bottom navigation and iOS status area without device-specific pixel assumptions.

rules.name: The Flat-Working-Surface Rule
rules.body: Do not use resting shadows, nested cards, glass effects, or decorative side stripes to manufacture hierarchy. Use content order, type, spacing, rules, and tonal fields first.

dos: Do foreground the family’s actual meals and next decision before planning mechanics or household administration.
Do use hierarchy, grouping, labels, and sensible defaults before adding instructional prose or configuration.
Do keep empty states subordinate to known meal content.
Do adapt information architecture for narrow screens, not merely shrink desktop layouts.
Do use warm editorial language only when it adds context without duplicating or replacing household state.
Do preserve original content while treating Spanish and English as equally complete supported experiences.
Do favor deletion, consolidation, and stronger defaults when a concept has not earned its cognitive cost.
donts: Don't expose implementation concepts, workflow terminology, or internal classifications unless the family truly needs to decide them.
Don't make an empty dinner imply that nothing else is planned today.
Don't flatten Day, Meal, and Recipe into equivalent typography or visual weight.
Don't squeeze complete multi-day meal content into narrow mobile columns.
Don't make users request a recipe-level translation after selecting the global language.
Don't elevate sides or minor components as complete dinner recommendations without supporting context.
Don't allow fixed navigation or device safe areas to obscure meaningful content or actions.
Don't turn warmth into verbose self-instruction or turn planning into a generic dashboard.
